title: Branch policy check at complete_task (consolidationBranch)
description: Objective: complete_task can verify the worker is on the sanctioned branch — settings.consolidationBranch (literal or glob); mismatch rejects with a BRANCH-POLICY-FAIL teaching error, missing currentBranch only warns #governors so wrapper rollout stays graceful. Deliverable: optional currentBranch param on complete_task + policy check. NOT in scope: wrapper changes (wrappers already peel to moe/work-*). Spec: item #9 in tag archive/governance-plane-v2. Verification command: npx vitest run src/tools/completeTask.test.ts
definitionOfDone: complete_task with matching currentBranch passes; mismatch rejects naming both branches
Missing currentBranch warns #governors and does not block
Unset consolidationBranch disables the check entirely

implementationPlan.description: Create `packages/moe-daemon/src/util/branchPolicy.ts` with the matcher, kept separate from the tool so it is unit-testable and has exactly one definition. Export `matchesBranchPattern(branch: string, pattern: string): boolean`: return false for an empty branch or empty pattern; when the pattern has no `*`, compare with strict equality; otherwise escape EVERY regex metacharacter in the pattern first (`.` `+` `?` `^` `$` `{` `}` `(` `)` `|` `[` `]` `\`), then replace the escaped `*` placeholders with `.*`, anchor with `^`/`$`, and test. Escaping before expanding is the whole point — a branch pattern like `release/v1.0-*` must not let `.` match any character, and an unescaped `(` would throw at compile time. Wrap the `new RegExp` in try/catch and return false on failure rather than throwing (error handling: a malformed pattern must not be able to crash `complete_task`). Also export `describeBranchPolicyFailure(branch, pattern): string` returning the teaching message body that names BOTH the branch the worker is on and the expected pattern, and tells them to switch to the sanctioned branch (or re-run the wrapper post-flight, which peels onto `moe/work-<date>`) and retry — keeping the wording in one place so the tool and its test cannot drift.
implementationPlan.note: Created packages/moe-daemon/src/util/branchPolicy.ts exporting matchesBranchPattern(branch, pattern) and describeBranchPolicyFailure(branch, pattern). Matcher: false for an empty branch or empty pattern; strict equality when the pattern has no `*`; otherwise escape every regex metacharacter first (which turns `*` into `\*`), then expand only those placeholders to `.*`, anchor ^/$ and test. new RegExp is wrapped in try/catch returning false, so a malformed pattern cannot crash complete_task (error handling). Case-sensitive by design. describeBranchPolicyFailure names both the actual branch and the expected pattern and points at the wrapper post-flight that peels onto moe/work-<date>, so the tool and its test share one wording. implementationPlan.description: Wire the check into `packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/completeTask.ts`. Add `currentBranch: { type: 'string', description: 'Branch the worker is on; enables the consolidationBranch policy check' }` to the input schema (still optional — wrappers that do not send it yet must keep working) and to the params type. Resolve the policy as `state.project?.settings?.consolidationBranch?.trim()`; when it is empty or unset, skip the whole block so unconfigured projects are completely unaffected. Place the check immediately AFTER `assertVerificationEvidence` and BEFORE the `state.updateTask` call so a rejection leaves the task untouched in WORKING. Three outcomes: (a) policy set and `currentBranch` provided and `matchesBranchPattern` true — proceed, and add `branchPolicy: { pattern, currentBranch, matched: true }` to the response; (b) policy set and `currentBranch` provided but not matching — throw a `MoeError` with code `CONSTRAINT_VIOLATION` whose message starts with `BRANCH-POLICY-FAIL:` followed by `describeBranchPolicyFailure(...)`, and whose data carries `{ currentBranch, expectedPattern }`; (c) policy set but `currentBranch` missing/empty — do NOT block (graceful wrapper rollout): post a one-line warning to `#governors` via `state.postToRoleChannel` inside its own try/catch, and return `branchPolicy: { pattern, matched: null, warning: 'currentBranch not reported — branch policy not enforced for this completion' }`. Leave verification enforcement, `filesModified` aggregation, the worker handoff, the activity log and `nextAction` untouched.
implementationPlan.note: Wired the policy into completeTask.ts: optional `currentBranch` added to the input schema and params type, and a module-level checkBranchPolicy(state, taskId, currentBranch) helper called immediately after assertVerificationEvidence and before state.updateTask, so a rejection leaves the task untouched in WORKING. Resolves the pattern as state.project?.settings?.consolidationBranch?.trim() and returns null when empty/unset — the response then carries no branchPolicy key at all, so unconfigured projects are untouched. Match -> { pattern, currentBranch, matched: true }; mismatch -> MoeError CONSTRAINT_VIOLATION with message 'BRANCH-POLICY-FAIL: ' + describeBranchPolicyFailure(...) and context { currentBranch, expectedPattern }; missing/whitespace currentBranch -> one-line warning to #governors via postToRoleChannel inside its own try/catch (it already swallows internally; wrapped anyway) and { pattern, matched: null, warning }. Naming note vs the plan: MoeError's third constructor argument is `context`, not `data` — the fields are exactly the two the plan named. Verification enforcement, filesModified aggregation, worker handoff, activity log and nextAction untouched. Verified: npx tsc --noEmit exit 0; npx vitest run src/tools/completeTask.test.ts -> 7 passed (existing cases unaffected). New policy cases land in step-5.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: (1) Having the daemon read the current branch itself via git — rejected here: the daemon's cwd is the project root, but the WORKER may be running elsewhere (WSL, a worktree), so the branch the daemon sees is not necessarily the branch the worker committed on. Taking it as a reported parameter keeps the check honest and matches the spec. (A sibling task in this epic does add a git helper for handoff disk state — do not conflate the two.) (2) Blocking when `currentBranch` is absent — explicitly rejected by the DoD: the wrappers do not send it yet, so a hard failure would break every completion on rollout. Warn-only is the graceful path. (3) Supporting a comma-separated list of allowed patterns — deferred: one glob covers the `moe/work-<date>` scheme the wrappers actually produce, and a list doubles the parsing and test surface for no current need. (4) Converting the glob with a naive `pattern.replace('*', '.*')` — rejected: unescaped metacharacters silently widen the match (`v1.0-*`) or throw at compile time.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights: `complete_task` is a pure validate-then-update handler: every assertion (`assertWorkerOwns`, `assertAllStepsCompleted`, `assertVerificationEvidence`) runs before the single `state.updateTask`, so adding the branch gate in that same pre-update band gives 'reject leaves the task untouched' for free — and the test should assert exactly that. `settings.qualityGate` is the precedent for a string setting whose empty value is the off switch, including its `validateStringValue(..., { allowEmpty: true, trim: true })` call — copy it rather than inventing new validation. Chat posting is best-effort everywhere (`postToRoleChannel` already swallows internally, but wrap anyway to match local style). The worker post-flight peels onto a shared `moe/work-<YYYY-MM-DD>` branch, which is why `moe/work-*` is the realistic pattern to document.
planningNotes.risks: 1) Glob-to-regex is the only real trap: escape metacharacters BEFORE expanding `*`, anchor both ends, and never let a malformed pattern throw out of the tool. 2) The rejection must happen before `updateTask` — a half-applied completion (task in REVIEW, worker still holding it) is much worse than a clean refusal. 3) Missing `currentBranch` must never block; the wrappers are out of scope for this task and will keep omitting it. 4) An empty-string `consolidationBranch` is the documented disable, so treat empty and unset identically — do not let `''` compile into a pattern that matches nothing and rejects every completion. 5) Case sensitivity is deliberate; do not lowercase either side. 6) Do not touch the JetBrains/VS Code settings dialogs — they expose a subset by design and adding a field there is a separate decision.
